column1: # Memory functions. One row per function, per task it belongs to. Tab-separated; see finder.py for the rules.

column7: summary
Reserves a number of bytes and returns a pointer to them, or 0; the bytes are not cleared.
Reserves memory for a number of elements, set to zero, and returns a pointer or 0.
Resizes a block, keeping its contents, and returns the new pointer, or 0 on failure.
Frees memory from Allocate, CAllocate or Reallocate; does nothing for a null pointer.
Returns a reference to the value at an address, as a byte or as a given type.
Writes a value to an address, as a byte or as a given type.
Returns a pointer to the characters of a string.
Copies a number of bytes between two memory areas that do not overlap.
Copies a number of bytes between two memory areas, even when they overlap.
Copies the first bytes of one area into another and sets the rest to zero.
Sets a number of bytes, starting at a variable, to zero or to a given value.
Exchanges the values of two variables.
Holds an object shared by several owners and destroys it when the last one lets go.
Creates a default-constructed object and returns the first SharedPtr to it.
Creates a copy of a value on the heap and returns a SharedPtr to it.
Returns how many SharedPtr handles share the object.
Drops this handle's share and leaves it null; the last one out destroys the object.
Returns a reference to the object; raises an error if the handle is null.
Returns the raw pointer to the object, or 0 if null, without adding an owner.
Returns true if the handle owns no object.
Returns a SharedPtr to a base type that shares ownership with the derived one.
Holds a link to a shared object that does not keep it alive, to break cycles.
Returns a SharedPtr to the object if it still exists, or a null one if not.
Returns true once the object has been destroyed.
